Dear Medical Director,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for Cervical Artificial Disc Replacement (ADR) for my patient {{patient_name}}. The Clinical Compass™ ADR Decision Support assessment yielded a recommendation of "[ADR Recommendation]" (Class of Recommendation [COR]) based on FDA approval criteria and NASS clinical guidelines.

CLINICAL JUSTIFICATION:
• Patient presents with symptomatic cervical disc disease with radiculopathy or myelopathy
• MRI evidence of disc herniation/degeneration with neural compression at [LEVEL(S)]
• Failure of ≥6 weeks conservative therapy documented
• Patient meets FDA-approved indications for cervical TDR

DIAGNOSIS:
• Primary diagnosis: Cervical degenerative disc disease with [radiculopathy / myelopathy]
• Level(s) involved: [e.g., C5-C6, C6-C7] — [single / two-level]
• Neurological symptoms: [DESCRIBE — arm pain, numbness, weakness, myelopathic symptoms]
• NDI Score: [SCORE]% (moderate disability 30-50%; severe >50%)

CONSERVATIVE THERAPY DOCUMENTATION:
This patient has completed a comprehensive course of conservative management including:
• Physical therapy / cervical traction: [DURATION — minimum 6 weeks, OUTCOMES]
• NSAIDs / analgesic medications: [MEDICATIONS, DURATION, RESPONSE]
• Cervical epidural steroid injections: [NUMBER, DATES, RESPONSE]
• Activity modification and cervical collar (if applicable): [DETAILS]

IMAGING FINDINGS:
• MRI cervical spine ({{letter_date}}): [DESCRIBE — disc herniation, foraminal stenosis, cord compression, disc height loss]
• CT cervical spine ({{letter_date}}, if applicable): [DESCRIBE — bony anatomy, osteophytes]
• Disc height loss: [PERCENTAGE] at [LEVEL(S)]
• Neural compression: [DESCRIBE — foraminal narrowing, cord signal change if myelopathy]

FDA-APPROVED INDICATIONS MET:
This patient meets all FDA-approved indications for cervical total disc replacement:
• Symptomatic cervical DDD at [1 or 2] level(s) between C3-C7
• Radiculopathy or myelopathy refractory to ≥6 weeks conservative therapy
• Skeletally mature patient (age [AGE])
• Absence of contraindications: no cervical instability, no significant osteoporosis, no active infection, no allergy to device materials
• Appropriate disc height preservation (>3mm) for device implantation

MEDICAL NECESSITY AND ADVANTAGE OVER FUSION:
Cervical ADR is medically necessary and preferred over ACDF for this patient because:
1. Motion preservation reduces adjacent segment degeneration — a known long-term complication of fusion
2. FDA-approved devices have demonstrated non-inferiority or superiority to ACDF in multiple Level I RCTs
3. Patient's age and activity level make motion preservation clinically advantageous
4. Long-term data (7+ years) demonstrate superior outcomes with TDR vs ACDF (Gornet et al., 2019)

GUIDELINE SUPPORT:
Multiple FDA-approved cervical disc replacement devices have demonstrated safety and efficacy in Level I randomized controlled trials with 7-10 year follow-up. NASS coverage policy supports cervical TDR for single or two-level cervical DDD with radiculopathy or myelopathy refractory to conservative care. The procedure is covered under CMS LCD L36920 when FDA-approved indications are met.

I respectfully request immediate reconsideration and approval of prior authorization for Cervical Artificial Disc Replacement. Please contact my office at {{practice_phone}} or {{practice_email}} if additional clinical documentation is required.

Sincerely,
